rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Chunk 8 'Optional challenges', line 71: 'route it to the right instruction surface'. HARM CHECK: the rule exists to keep repo/maintainer authoring vocabulary off a wall a room reads cold; 'surface' used as a bare noun ('an X surface' = a place instructions live) is the compendium's OWN named banned example ('surface as noun ("writing surface")'), and the exact phrase pattern recurs verbatim in this repo's internal planning doc (curriculum/module-design/ae101-m6-pipeline-deltas.md:47, '(writing surface)'), confirming it is house authoring jargon and not ordinary engineer-register vocabulary -- the rule's own register carve-out explicitly excludes 'surface'-as-noun even for AE101's engineer audience ('unlike compendium / surface-as-noun which are genuinely repo-internal'). Checked the exception clauses: this is not the ordinary-verb use ('surface the issue'), not a canonical section name, not a locked-file authoring scheme, and not a rule quoted as a specimen -- it is communicating an instruction to the student, which is exactly what §8's test fires on. The harm (a room reading a term the repo invented, with no referent to a real, nameable artefact -- which of CLAUDE.md / CLAUDE.local.md / a skill file is 'the right instruction surface'?) is present. Not a diff-introduced regression -- unchanged since a0449afa, where it was apparently missed on the prior slides pass at the identical pin. No maintainer accept-note in the block (lines 88-185) names this phrase.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Name the real thing instead of the abstraction -- 'route it to the right rules file' or 'to CLAUDE.md, CLAUDE.local.md, or a skill file, whichever fits' -- something the student can point at.
